title: surface-capabilities v1
description: What one surface says it can do, as data: surfaces/<name>/capabilities.json (decisions design 2026-10-06, decision 2). A surface shows a page that Horde owns - in a window, later in a file or across a link - and carries the page's requests to Horde; it knows nothing of what the page is about. Each capability is declared in the one vocabulary the host, transport and messenger capability files use - yes, no, declined or unverified - with its evidence; unverified counts as no, and a capability is yes only with evidence that was run. The list is closed: a surface declares every one, and nothing else.

page.local.description: The page is loaded from folders on this machine with no web server and no listening port, so nothing else on the machine or the network can reach it.

page.locked.description: The page cannot leave: a navigation anywhere but the page's own folders is refused, and so is a request for a new window.

requests.closed.description: The page and Horde talk only through the closed list of named requests of surfaces/Port.ps1, each checked on arrival; the page is handed no object of Horde's to call.

push.description: Horde can hand the page a named event while it is shown, so the page redraws without being reloaded.

window.native.description: The surface is a window of this machine with a native handle, which a window follower can own and place beside another window.

picture.description: Horde can ask the surface to save a picture of the page exactly as it is drawn, so that what a person would see can be looked at without that person. Only Horde can ask: it is not one of the page's requests.

evidence.description: What was run or read, and when. Never blank.
